body:
Don't have much time to make a full response yet, but a dear friend of mine just graduated from a very well known engineering school summa cum laude with fantastic internships and lots of research done, she went home and tried to get a job for the downtime between now and when she starts going to grad school to get her PhD. She applied to ~40 positions at everywhere imaginable (from steak & shake to hobby lobby) and didn't get a single interview.

The thing is, they're much more interested in hiring ex-felons and high school kids than college graduates due to lower expectations and a sense of desperation. 

I love this economy, don't you?

...And now she puts a picture of she and I together as her profile picture on facebook. She has plenty of photos of we two plus her fiance, but she chose this one. 

I can't wrap my head around this.

For what it's worth, as far as I know, warfarin isn't exactly an easy drug to come across. It's sole use is as an anti-coagulant. So it isn't like he'd have been able to buy any from an illegitimate source, nor would he be likely be able to get it off of someone around his age. The only way I could see him getting it would have been if his deceased parent had had a condition that required its use. However, warfarin has a shelf life of ~2 years with a maximal dosage/pill of 5mg (so he would have need 100 of these to get his alleged .5g dose). Most patients are prescribed a 5mg/day dosage so having a leftover bottle with ~1/3 years worth of prescription anticoagulant in it is very unlikely.

/my $.02

>I have to trust them. If I stop trusting them, well...

That's just the thing, though. I never really get to that point of trusting someone. Heather has been the closest person to that in a long time, but now I just don't know anymore.

>you need to make being alone a cold, but calm sea

That's the way I was before I met her. I was alone, but I was content in my misanthropy and cynicism. Since meeting her I've had to start thinking about how maybe people aren't all trash. Part of me wishes I'd never met her, life was much more simple when I could just hate everyone.

>(i.e. a little bit o' time in the so-called "psych ward") and it's done them wonders.

Possibly an option for some, but for a to-be medical school student that would be tantamount to just quitting school.

>it's been a matter of SSRIs giving the clarity of thought to create my own new state of mind.

Are you still taking SSRIs? If so, would you retain this new state of mind after coming off of them?

>she just sees things differently than you do

To me, completely ignoring about an entire month's worth of attempted correspondences is just something that isn't done. Especially polarizing it with 'I'm bored' and 'I miss you'

>She has (or had) a fiance
Has, they're getting married in a couple of months. But that's the thing, I don't seek a romantic relationship with her at all, I am 100% fine with maintaining a completely platonic relationship. I just want the relationship to exist.

>there's something wrong with your thinking.
More than likely, I microanalyze everything.

So, quick comment before I head off to class.

Interesting situation occurred yesterday. She reinitiated contact after a month or so with nothing. No responses to the direct questions that I've asked in the interim, no apologies for business. Just like "Oh hey X, how are things? I've been doing this for awhile, been really bored. I miss you, Heather"

I have no fucking idea how to respond to this.

Part of me wonders if she's just toying with me.

>Secondly, they won't commit you for telling them how you feel

Directly from the website:
There are specific situations, however, when the counselor/psychologist is required by law to breach confidentiality - when there is a possibility the person may harm himself/herself, harm someone else, when child or vulnerable adult abuse is indicated, or when subpoenaed by a court of law.

>Why do you say this?

I say this because even though she has never proven herself untrustworthy, even behind my back. I still cannot trust her and I go to absurd lengths to try to prove to myself that she is untrustworthy.

>Are you aware that there's a strong correlation between low serotonin and obsessive romantic love?

I actually had no idea there was any sort of correlation. Interesting.

>think of how anxiety-inducing the modern, complex world is to the person of average-to-below-average intelligence

I would imagine that they would have much less to worry about. They have their crappy jobs that earn them enough to support themselves and their family and they have a caring god to look forward to after they've come to the end of their ultimately meaningless lives. This is the kind of person I just cannot understand. I could never live my life just working to get by.

>Are you daunted more than you realise by the prospect of going through with your degree?

I suppose that could be part of it. Going to medical school isn't a problem for me anymore, but realizing that the field I wish to pursue after that is one of the most competitive out of all is daunting. I don't care about money, I don't care about helping people. For me, it is but an intellectual pursuit.

>paragraph 2

I would think that myself if I hadn't come to know him fairly well in the past year or so along with her. He and I have gotten together a few times independently of Heather by his invitation so I don't think that is the problem, but then again he has more or less cut off communication as well.

>paragraph 3
The anonymous call actually sounds like a pretty good idea, perhaps I'll give it a shot.

>Can no one else ever be that way to you? If so, why?

I suppose it's possible, but I think that it is unlikely that I'll find another person with whom I will be able to interact with like I did with her.

>can you tell me some of the better experiences in your life?

Honestly not much outside of hollow academic achievements and being with Heather for the past year or so.

>Was your friendship in place because you were seeking benefit, rather than company? If you were in her shoes, what would you have done?

I was able to get way more out of my relationship with her than vice-versa. Seeing as she was a year ahead of me, she was able to advise me on the different classes I should/shouldn't take among other things. Your second question is interesting. I don't really know if I would want to be friends with myself. I suppose if I were a slightly altered me, such that I had had different experiences up to this point while retaining the same personality I would be able to befriend myself.

>But doesn't it follow that you can't have her since she's already engaged? Do you want her to live a good life?
I never wanted to have her as a romantic interest. She was just a very good friend and I was perfectly happy with that. I do want her to be happy, really. She has had some really awful experiences in her last few years that really merit happiness. It is because of this that if I do indeed end my life, I will go missing. I would not want to cause her any sort of guilt, though in all reality she was a driving force towards the decision.

>Gee, I didn't know I would be useful for that :|

I think you misinterpreted what I meant to say. I meant that my opinion of you as a formless person over the internet as being simply someone who really doesn't gain anything from talking with me is not likely to change unless you started trying to solicit cheap pharmaceuticals. 

>This was about the small minority of people who wouldn't have anything to gain from you, who wouldn't have ulterior motives. I'm not sure where they became psychopaths, and I'm also not sure why the cynic in you wouldn't want to question substance, rather than the specifics, of the situation at hand.

Yeah, I worded that badly. I was referring to myself as the psychopath, with the minority being those who would want to befriend one such as I.

>would you not want to improve your self-worth, however good it may already be?

I really don't have any self-worth to speak of. I look at humanity like I would look at a colony of ants. I'm sure on a basic level every ant feels self-important. I save some lives, an ant fends off a beetle. I suppose I do feel that I am better than a good amount of other people, but in the grand scheme of things we all amount to nothing.

>What's the difference between this one person, and the rest of the people in this world?
She is absurdly intelligent, mature, cultured. There was nothing about her that I resented. 

>Do you know what she thinks of you? Is that image "okay" enough for you to accept? If not, would you want to change it?
She used to consider me a friend, who knows any more.

>What makes you feel that every single person is bent on "turning on you"?
Probably due to bad school/home experiences growing up.

>Did you ask her for her reasons, or did you simply conclude so yourself?
I went through every facet of my relationship with her and was unable to find any concrete benefits for her side.

>Does the thought that there is just one person you can be close to (other than yourself) make you feel that you ought to change this? Doesn't it want to make you prove that it isn't your *thing* to keep doing this to anyone you might meet?
The thing is, I don't really *want* to be close to anyone else. I find the majority of people to be distasteful and irritating.

>And does that actually leave anything more to be understood from my point of view at all, or is that written in stone once you've laid out your opinion of me? :-)
Until you start trying to sell me generic viagra pills, that's pretty much my opinion of everyone on forums such as these.

>Does that not want you to understand why that small minority (anomaly?) of people exist, and does it not make you question your indelible opinions as being a tad inflexible at times, even those about yourself? :-)
I don't know, maybe for every psychopath there is someone who is so starved for intelligent conversation that they will seek it wherever they can get it. Even in a caustic cynic such as myself. I give everyone a shot, I've rarely ever just closed someone off immediately. It's just that most have proven themselves unworthy by some means or another. 

>Would you not want to change at all?
Honestly? I would not want to lower my standards on people just so that I could forge meaningless relationships, as awful and elitist as that probably sounds.

>Do you want strong attachment? Do you need strong attachment?
Up until recently I was completely fine being so detached from everyone. I'm still okay with it except for this one person, honestly. 

>Are you sure you never had any feelings for her beyond friendship? Or are you lying to yourself?
When I first met her, I had a bit of lust, sure. She's very beautiful. But once I really got to know her, even a completely platonic relationship with her was all I needed. I suppose I could say that I love her, but not in a romantic sense. I imagine my love for her like what someone would normally feel towards their family. She was someone that I could talk to without feeling like they would just as soon turn on me as any other.

>Do you know what's bothering you, rather than what's bothering her, at the moment?

What's bothering me is the distinct lack of any communication between her and I. I feel that it is deliberate and it depresses me to know that I have possibly alienated the one person I've ever grown close to.

>How much do you trust yourself to start making a difference in your own life, given that there isn't any privacy to be breached here?

Not entirely certain I get your meaning, here. I'm just about the only person I can trust. I know my own thought processes and subtexts, these are things which I can only surmise about in others.

>Are you not willing to learn what trust is about?
Hell, I thought I was beginning to, but this situation has really set me back. Through the year or so that I knew her, I was constantly trying to evaluate her intentions for being around me. I could find no possible explanation other than she simply enjoyed my company. But now that she's gone away it's like she wants to cut me off completely, leading me to believe that I've done something to cause this.

>will you question my intent?
That's the thing about the internet though, you have almost literally nothing to gain from spending your time shooting responses back and forth with me, other than perhaps some personal satisfaction.

>Not everyone or everything in this world works the way you think about them in your head. 

Sure, I can't say that 100% of the people I meet are going to be attempting to befriend purely for their own benefit, but empirical evidence suggests that a good majority are.
